# Design system - frontend guidelines
# [frontend only] Read before building or changing any UI. Keeps pages visually coherent.
# RULE: the real tokens live in code (tailwind.config / theme.ts / CSS vars; or Compose theme / res-values).
#       This file documents usage rules and points at those tokens - it does NOT duplicate their values,
#       so they can't drift. Put machine-checkable rules (no raw hex, use components) into lint in test.cjs.
#
# v2 (feature 012): replaces the Apple-minimal system from feature 002 with the "Precision
# Engineering & Inclusive Craft" system generated by Stitch (see
# stitch_qa_accessibility_portfolio_redesign/DESIGN.md for the original AI-generated spec — this
# file is the corrected, implemented version; some values/claims from that spec were adjusted or
# dropped, see notes.md for what and why).

## Tokens - source of truth
Where the real values live (edit this pointer, not copies of the values):
- Colors: `src/index.css` (`@theme` block for dark defaults, `:root` for light, `[data-theme="dark"]`
  override — Tailwind v4, no `tailwind.config.js`)
- Typography scale: `src/index.css` `@theme` block, `--text-headline-*` / `--text-body-*` /
  `--text-code-*` / `--text-label-*` (Tailwind v4 bundled size+line-height+letter-spacing+weight).
  Font families: `--font-sans` (Inter) and `--font-mono` (JetBrains Mono), loaded via Google Fonts
  `<link>` in `index.html` — use the plain `font-sans`/`font-mono` Tailwind utilities, not per-size
  family tokens (the Stitch export had one fontFamily per size; every headline/body size maps to
  Inter and every code/label size to JetBrains Mono, so overriding the two Tailwind defaults is
  equivalent and simpler — don't reintroduce per-size family tokens).
- Spacing scale: Tailwind default spacing scale (no custom override).
- Dark mode: `src/contexts/ThemeProvider.tsx` toggles `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`; light is the
  `:root` default, dark values live under `[data-theme="dark"]` in `src/index.css`.

## Colors - usage (Material-3-shaped roles)
Each color has a base role (text/icon on a surface) and a `-container` role (a filled surface with
its own `on-*-container` text):
- `primary` / `on-primary` / `primary-container` / `on-primary-container`: Electric Cobalt. `primary`
  is text/icon accent on a surface (eyebrows, links, active nav state); `primary-container` is the
  solid fill for primary CTAs, with `on-primary-container` as its label color.
- `secondary` / `on-secondary` / `secondary-container` / `on-secondary-container`: Signal Emerald.
  Success/pass states, secondary accents.
- `tertiary` / `on-tertiary` / `tertiary-container` / `on-tertiary-container`: Vivid Chartreuse.
  Diagnostic/highlight accent — use sparingly, it's the loudest color in the palette.
- `error` / `on-error` / `error-container` / `on-error-container`: reserved, not used yet (no forms).
- Neutrals: `surface` (page background) → `surface-container-lowest` → `surface-container-low` →
  `surface-container` → `surface-container-high` → `surface-container-highest` (each a progressively
  more "raised" panel — a `Card` sits on `surface-container`, a bento tile inside it can go one step
  higher). `on-surface` / `on-surface-variant` are body text / muted text. `outline` / `outline-variant`
  are for icons-that-need-a-border and hairline borders, respectively.
Rule: never hardcode a hex in a component. Use the token.

## Typography
- Two families by intent, not by size: `font-sans` (Inter) for narrative/UI text (headings, body,
  labels), `font-mono` (JetBrains Mono) for anything diagnostic/technical (dates, tech tags, status
  pills, nav links, metrics) — this duality is a signature of the redesign, keep it consistent.
- Scale: `text-headline-xl/lg/md/sm` for headings (xl = H1 only), `text-body-lg/md/sm` for prose,
  `text-code-lg/md/sm` and `text-label-md/sm` for mono/technical text (labels are uppercase +
  wide-tracked, set via the token itself — don't add `uppercase tracking-*` again on top).
- Rule: one H1 per page (the hero name). Section titles are H2. Never skip a heading level.
- Line heights are baked into each `text-*` token already (≥1.4×) — don't override.

## Spacing & layout
- Spacing unit: Tailwind's default 4px-based scale — no arbitrary px values in components.
- Container max width: `max-w-5xl` for prose-driven sections, up to `max-w-7xl`/full-bleed with
  `px-gutter`-equivalent padding (`px-6 sm:px-8`) for grid/bento layouts.
- Breakpoints: Tailwind defaults (`sm md lg xl`) — mobile-first. Dense grids (bento, skill matrix)
  collapse to a single column below `lg`.
- Interactive tap targets never below 44×44px (WCAG 2.2 target size) — already enforced in `Button`/
  `ButtonToogle`; keep it when adding new interactive elements (icon-only buttons, card link areas).

## Shapes & elevation
- Radius: `rounded` (0.25rem) is the default for cards/inputs/tags; `rounded-lg` (0.5rem) for larger
  grouping containers; `rounded-full` for pills/badges/avatars.
- Depth via **tonal layering + borders**, not diffuse shadows: a raised panel is a lighter/darker
  `surface-container-*` step plus a 1px `border-outline-variant`, not a `shadow-*` utility. Reserve
  `shadow-*` for true overlays (modals, dropdowns) if any are ever added — none exist yet.

## Components - reuse, do not re-roll
Canonical components that MUST be reused instead of hand-built (`src/components/`):
- `controls/Button.tsx` (primary = filled `primary-container`, secondary = bordered `surface-container`
  + `font-mono` label), `controls/ButtonLink.tsx`, `controls/ButtonToogle.tsx`, `cards/Card.tsx`
  (`surface-container` + `border-outline-variant`), `placing/Row.tsx` / `Column.tsx` (+ `Inverted`).
Rule: if a primitive exists, use it. New shared primitives go in `src/components/`, not inline in a page.

## States
No data-fetching in this project (static content from the CV) — no loading/empty/error states needed.
The only stateful UI is the dark-mode toggle (persisted) and scroll-reveal animations (see below).

## Interaction & accessibility
- Focus states: `2px solid` outline in `--color-primary` + `2px` offset, global via `a:focus-visible,
  button:focus-visible` in `index.css` — never `outline-none` without that replacement.
- Hover/active: subtle (opacity/background-step shift), consistent ~200ms `ease-out`.
- Motion: scroll-reveal via `IntersectionObserver` (`useScrollReveal`, no library) — fade + small
  translate-Y; a global `prefers-reduced-motion` reset in `index.css` collapses all transitions/
  animations site-wide, on top of `useScrollReveal` skipping its observer outright under that
  preference.
- Skip-link: `#main-content` skip-link is the first focusable element (feature 013) — keep it working
  when touching `Page.tsx`/`Header.tsx`.
- A11y baseline (user is a professional accessibility QA — hold this to a high bar): WCAG AA contrast
  minimum on all text/background pairs (both themes — see notes.md for the light-theme contrast
  reasoning), semantic landmarks (`nav`, `main`, `footer`), descriptive link text (no bare "aquí"),
  `alt` text on any meaningful image, accessible name on every icon-only control.
- **Never state an unverified compliance/certification claim** (e.g. "WCAG 2.2 AAA VERIFIED" as if
  audited, "ISTQB Certified", a specific live test-pass count) — the site can describe principles it
  follows and skills the user has, but not present fabricated audit results as fact. See notes.md.

## Voice / UI copy
- Tone: profesional pero cercano/humano, en español. Frases cortas, sin jerga corporativa vacía.
  Los CTAs son claros y directos ("Descargar CV", "Contactar"), no genéricos ("Haz clic aquí").
- Technical/diagnostic copy (terminal widgets, metric tiles, tech tags) can lean into the "dev tool"
  voice the redesign introduces, but must stay truthful — see the a11y rule above.
